lineage.strategy: Use fresh issuer results to separate strong reported execution from forward project-timing and acquisition-attribution risks.

observedWeaknesses.observation: Quanta raised full-year expectations after strong Q2 results but explicitly identified weather, regulatory, permitting, supply-chain, inflation, interest-rate and recession exposures; the release does not fully isolate recent-acquisition contribution from organic execution.
observedWeaknesses.whyItMatters: Large project execution remains sensitive to external timing and cost variables, while acquisition contribution can complicate interpretation of underlying organic momentum.

risks.risk: Raised guidance remains exposed to project timing, permitting, supply-chain and macro conditions, and headline growth can overstate organic execution if acquisition contribution is not separated.

falsifiers.condition: Subsequent source-addressed results sustain cash generation and margins while separately demonstrating strong organic growth and stable project conversion despite the cited external risks.
falsifiers.effect: Would reduce timing and acquisition-attribution concerns.

improvementPaths: Separate organic and acquisition-driven contribution and continue demonstrating backlog-to-cash conversion under permitting and supply-chain variability.

unknowns.unknown: Incremental margin and return contribution from recent acquisitions versus organic execution is not fully isolated in the cited release.

recommendation: Use as bounded project-timing and attribution risk evidence; Alpha retains numeric risk and score authority.
